findings.title: Standalone verifier report publication follows symlinks and permits destructive input overlap
findings.description: After verification succeeds, the CLI passes the caller-controlled --report path directly to std::fs::write. Existing files are truncated, existing symlinks are followed, and the parser permits --report to equal --image or --result. Thus a successful invocation can destroy the just-verified input or replace another user-writable symlink target and still return success.
findings.impact: Local integrity/availability footgun and a conventional shared-directory symlink hazard. Verification and replay decisions remain correct before the write; stdout mode is unaffected. Exploitation requires the invoking user's path choice or an untrusted report directory, so this review rates the issue low rather than medium.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the executor's no-replace publication pattern: require a real parent directory; create and sync a new temporary file in that directory; publish without replacement; remove staging; sync the parent. Reject an existing report path, any path overlap with image/result, and any report path inside the tensor store. Add existing-file, symlink, hard-link, input-overlap, and interrupted-publication tests.

findings.title: Packaged core documentation points to normative contract and threat-model documents absent from the signed closure
findings.description: The core document identifies EXECUTION_CONTRACT_V1.md as normative and THREAT_MODEL.md as the location of risks and exclusions, but neither file exists anywhere in the 68-file signed candidate. The package does contain substantial boundary language in README.md, docs/FAILPOINT-BOUNDARY.md, and the standalone verifier README, so this review found no direct contradiction; the gap primarily limits standalone auditability.
findings.impact: A recipient cannot recover the named normative contract or complete broader threat model from the authenticated archive alone.
findings.recommendation: Include checksum-bound copies of both named documents in the next candidate, or change the signed documentation to point only to the boundary documents actually present.
